correctness.rationale: One step maps every plane point to diagonal scalar s=q(x,y), which is bounded below by −1/300; future scalar recurrence g(s)=s/5+3s² has only 0 and r=4/15 fixed, and g(s)−s=s(3s−4/5). Negative s increase to 0, 0<s<r decrease to 0, and s>r increase unboundedly. Completing squares makes q<r a centered positive-definite ellipse; area equals (2π/√3)(r+1/300)=9√3π/50. The claimed radius r is the exact maximal centered sup norm box, because (r,r) is excluded. Poincaré recurrence confines an invariant probability to two actual fixed points. For uniform area on r<q<H, quadratic level-set area is affine in s, hence s is uniform. Inverse h(t)=(√(1+300t)−1)/30 on [r,∞) gives P(N_H>n)=(h^n(H)−r)/(H−r). Inverse expansion at r yields λ=5/9 and a convergent positive product for sharp exponential tails; a tail telescoping bound gives dTV≤125(H−r)/48. Independently verified scalar, area, inverse derivative and multiplier identities. No finite data proves global assertions.
